transfers.source_mechanism: Resource flow enables structural adaptation under feedback regulation, producing optimized network topology
transfers.target_problem: A mid-sized city (population 800,000) has a traffic signal network with 247 signalized intersections. The current signal timing plan is optimized centrally every 6 months using a macroscopic traffic model, but it cannot adapt to real-time conditions: incidents, weather, special events, and construction. Re-optimizing centrally every minute is computationally infeasible and would require expensive predictive models. The city wants a distributed, adaptive signal timing approach that uses only local traffic flow measurements (vehicle count and queue length at each intersection) to adjust green-split and offset in real time, without a central optimizer.
transfers.transferred_principle: Adaptive network systems optimize resource distribution through dynamic structural modification based on usage patterns.
transfers.required_translation: Replace resource flow with traffic flow, structural adaptation with signal timing adjustments, and network topology with traffic signal coordination. Replace rhythmic contraction with signal cycle adjustments, structural thickening with increased green time for congested approaches, structural thinning with decreased green time for underutilized approaches, and self-repair with automatic offset recalibration based on queue dissipation.
transfers.expected_effect: Distributed optimization of traffic signal timing that adapts to real-time conditions without central coordination, reducing overall travel time and improving network efficiency.
boundary_conditions: Local measurements only (vehicle count and queue length)
transfers.testable_prediction: After implementing the adaptive signal system, average travel time during a non-recurring incident will decrease by at least 15% within 20 minutes without central re-optimization, compared to the current system.
